correctness_confidence.basis: Hand-rechecked Thm 1 (Jensen/Blaschke/Mahler chain, constant), Mathieu expansion giving 1/8 in Thm 5, Prop 18 algebra, Prop 14 constant: consistent. Lemma 6/7/Prop 8, Lemma 6.2, Thm 4/13 only skimmed; external Mathieu asymptotics unchecked.

rigor.basis: Proofs are mostly explicit with displayed inequalities. Thm 5 lower-bound minimisation (uniformity of Mathieu remainder, minimiser window) and Thm 4 implicit-function step are terse; existential constants and non-explicit M_A, C_A, N_A are openly stated.

novelty.basis: Results extend Tan et al. [1] (v3 arXiv, Aug 2026) and Luo et al. [2]: arbitrary slope, sqrt(n) without log, interior-zero budget classification, one-root threshold. Methods largely adapted from [1],[11]. Priority not certified by the author; I could not check sources.

significance.basis: Gives a sharp zero-count dichotomy (b_n to infinity iff superalgebraic decay) and 1/sqrt8 circle barrier. Niche subfield; rate gaps remain (n^-1/6 vs n^-13/6, exp(-C sqrt n) lower bound only, no upper bound).

reproducibility.basis: Analytic arguments are self-contained; supplementary diagnostics are described (60-digit solves, grids to 1e7) but not provided in the PDF, so I could not run or check them. Author candidly notes AI-assisted checks are non-independent.

summary: The manuscript studies residuals ||P'-lambda P||_2/||P||_2 for polynomials with zeros in the closed disk. It proves a quantitative lower bound in terms of the number M of interior zeros (Thm 1), an exact criterion b_n to infinity for superalgebraic decay under an interior-zero budget (Thm 2), exp(-C sqrt n) lower bounds for unrestricted s_n (Thm 3), the limit 1/sqrt8 for circle-only zeros (Thm 5), and existence of one-interior-zero families with residual O(n^-1/6) (Thm 13, constant in Prop 14) with a universal n^-13/6 lower bound (Prop 18). My partial hand verification of the Thm 1 chain, the Mathieu minimisation giving 1/8, Prop 14 and Prop 18 found no error. The heavier constructions (Lemma 6, 6.2, Thm 4, 13) were not fully verified, and external dependencies [1],[2] could not be checked. Claims are modest and limits are stated honestly.
strengths: Theorem 1 proof is short and checks out: Blaschke/Poisson positivity on a semicircle plus Jensen and a Mahler-type multiplication bound give an explicit bound for every M.
Mathieu-based lower bound for circle-root residuals reproduces the claimed limit 1/8 in the squared residual (my algebra agrees), matching the explicit upper family.
Prop 18 (one interior zero, n^-13/6) is elementary and the moment algebra verified in my check.
Honest scope statements: non-sharpness, existential constants, prior art and non-independent AI checks are disclosed.
weaknesses: Heavy dependence on recent arXiv preprints [1],[2] whose results are reused (normalisation, projected Newton identity, Erdos 973 refinement); correctness inherits from them.
Theorem 4 and Theorem 2 sufficiency are existential: no explicit M_A, C_A, N_A, so the classification has no quantitative threshold.
Large gap between lower exponent 13/6 and constructed 1/6 for one interior zero; general lower bound exp(-C sqrt n) has no matching upper bound.
Several steps (Thm 5 uniform minimisation, Lemma 12 rational kernel vector, implicit-function step) are compressed; numerical support is described but not included.
potential_errors: Thm 5 lower bound: uniformity of the displayed Mathieu remainder O(n^-1) over the window (n+1)lambda ~ n^2 is asserted from DLMF (28.8.1), which is an asymptotic in fixed-order sense; uniformity in L should be justified.
Prop 14 final display writes the limit of sqrt(n)||G_n||_2^2 as 1/sqrt(2) in the rendered text vs 1/sqrt(2 pi) implied by the Gaussian integral; likely typographical.
Lemma 7 radius-r disk extends outside the closed unit disk; the coefficient bound E(1+u) used there is valid but sensitive to q<=1/2 condition in Cor/Thm 3 choices; not independently re-derived.
strong_novelty_candidates: Exact characterisation: superalgebraic decay of the residual is possible iff the number of interior zeros tends to infinity (Theorem 2).
One interior zero already breaks the 1/sqrt8 circle barrier, with residual O(n^-1/6) and a universal n^-13/6 lower bound (Thm 13, Prop 18).
